state:
- The prediction that phospho-null protection will be only 'partial' rests on S4-mediated impairment being 'phosphorylation-independent' — an inference, not packet support; sequestration could also act on phosphorylated pores. Fix: add this as a declared assumption and calibrate the expected SG-only component by measuring transport decline under matched stress in phospho-null neurons before using 'partial vs full' protection as an interpretive criterion.
- The Phase 0 gate (pore-localized phospho-occupancy rising before import decline) is the linchpin of the program but transient, low-stoichiometry NPC phosphorylation is explicitly admitted to be below MS detection limits, which could make the gate fail spuriously or select by detection artefact. Fix: pre-specify an enrichment scheme (phosphopeptide enrichment of crosslinked/enriched nuclear envelopes) plus orthogonal validation (site-validated phospho-antibodies) with a defined occupancy threshold, otherwise the advance rule is uninterpretable.
- The 'selective TNPO1-dependent import decline' discriminator assumes phosphorylated Nup98 GLFG repeats dock karyopherins selectively, but GLFG motifs interact with multiple karyopherins; a failure of cargo-selective decline would be ambiguous between A5 failure and a generic facilitated-import defect. Fix: benchmark the phospho- vs phospho-null FG-domain constructs against comparator FG domains (Nup153/Nup50) and include total facilitated-import flux as a co-primary readout so the selectivity prediction is attributable to the modified domain rather than reporter choice.
